I do not assume the existence of the universe has a further reason behind it. I think reality includes brute facts, even if identifying a particular one is difficult.
</excerpt>
<excerpt id="E2" written="2023-04">
I think some facts simply have no explanation. At some point reality just is a certain way, and asking why does not guarantee there is an answer waiting.
</excerpt>
<excerpt id="E3" written="2023-06">
An endless demand for reasons does not convince me that reasons are always available. My view is that some facts really are inexplicable, rather than merely unexplained so far.
</excerpt>
<excerpt id="E4" written="2025-10">
I am wondering how someone could defend the claim that absolutely every fact has an explanation. Would that require an endless chain, or could a final explanation account for itself too?
</excerpt>
